title: Brushed DC Electric Motor
overview: Classic electromagnetic actuator converting direct current electrical energy into mechanical rotational torque via Lorenz magnetic force on armature coils.
learningObjectives: Observe mechanical commutation between stationary carbon brushes and rotating commutator segments
Trace Lorentz force generation across copper armature windings in a fixed magnetic field
Analyze back-EMF opposing voltage generation as angular rotational velocity increases
Inspect magnetic flux paths through permanent ferrite field magnets and steel flux casing

components.name: Steel Stator Housing & Flux Ring
components.summary: Ferromagnetic low-carbon steel cylindrical can serving as structural chassis and external magnetic flux return path.
components.howItWorks: Completes the magnetic circuit between the North and South permanent field magnets, shielding stray EMI and preventing flux leakage.
components.whyNeeded: Without the ferromagnetic return ring, magnetic flux density across the air gap drops dramatically, slashing motor torque.

components.name: Permanent Field Magnets (N-S Pair)
components.summary: Dual curved ceramic ferrite permanent magnets providing stationary radial magnetic flux lines across the armature core.
components.howItWorks: Creates a continuous magnetic field (B-field) directed perpendicular to the rotating armature copper wires.
components.whyNeeded: Essential for Lorentz force interaction: F = I * (L x B). Without a stator field, no torque is generated.

components.name: Laminated Armature Rotor Core
components.summary: Stack of insulated thin electrical steel laminations slotted to hold the copper armature windings.
components.howItWorks: Concentrates magnetic flux lines through the coils while minimizing parasitic eddy current induction losses.
components.whyNeeded: Solid steel cores would generate massive circular eddy currents, overheating the motor and wasting battery power.
keyFacts: 3-pole skewed slot profile to reduce cogging torque

components.name: Copper Armature Coil Windings
components.summary: Heavy-gauge enameled magnet wire wound into 3 separate armature coils connected to the commutator segments.
components.howItWorks: Carries DC electrical current through the magnetic field, producing rotational tangential torque on the shaft.
components.whyNeeded: Current passing through wires in a magnetic field experiences Lorentz force, turning electrical energy into mechanical work.
keyFacts: Dynamic precision balanced with epoxy balancing putty

components.name: 3-Segment Copper Commutator
components.summary: Cylindrical copper contact ring split into three electrically isolated segments by thin mica dielectric sheets.
components.howItWorks: Rotates with the shaft to mechanically reverse current direction in each coil as it crosses the magnetic neutral plane.
components.whyNeeded: Without polarity reversal every half-turn, torque would reverse and the rotor would lock in static alignment instead of spinning.
keyFacts: High-conductivity copper with silver alloy plating
Diamond-turned surface finish for brush longevity

components.name: Carbon Brushes & Torsion Springs
components.summary: Conductive spring-loaded graphite contact blocks sliding against the spinning commutator surface.
components.howItWorks: Transfers external DC electrical power from stationary terminals into the rapidly spinning armature coils.
components.whyNeeded: Provides a robust sliding electrical bridge between stationary battery wiring and rotating rotor electronics.
keyFacts: Electrographite composite with low friction coefficient
Beryllium copper coil preload springs (approx. 2.2 N force)

components.name: Hardened Steel Drive Shaft
components.summary: Ground stainless steel center axle transmitting rotor mechanical power to external pinions or gearboxes.
components.howItWorks: Locks the armature core, commutator, and cooling fan onto a single precision-balanced rotational axis.
components.whyNeeded: Transfers internal electromagnetic torque outward to drive wheels, propellers, or robotic joints.
keyFacts: Machined D-flat for set screw clamping

components.name: Precision Ball Bearings (Front & Rear)
components.summary: Deep-groove shielded radial ball bearings supporting the shaft with minimal rotational friction.
components.howItWorks: Houses chrome steel balls between inner and outer raceways lubricated with synthetic high-speed grease.
components.whyNeeded: Absorbs radial and axial loads while keeping the armature precisely centered in the narrow stator air gap.

components.name: Rear End Bell & Terminals
components.summary: Molded heat-resistant nylon cap housing the brush holders, suppression capacitors, and spade power terminals.
components.howItWorks: Holds brush alignment relative to the commutator and seals the rear bearing cavity.
components.whyNeeded: Provides rigid insulated mounting for electrical power inputs.

connections.label: DC Current Input (+ / -)
connections.description: DC voltage connected to terminals passes through internal copper shunts to the carbon brushes.

connections.label: Sliding Contact Current Transfer
connections.description: Mechanical sliding electrical contact transferring current into the rotating commutator segments.

connections.label: Commutated Armature Phase
connections.description: Current directed into the specific coil currently aligned with the magnetic field.

connections.label: Magnetic Torque Transfer
connections.description: Tangential electromagnetic Lorentz force transfers to the laminated steel core teeth.

connections.label: Press-Fit Shaft Torque
connections.description: Interference press-fit transmits core rotation directly to the center drive shaft.

connections.label: Convective Heat Dissipation
connections.description: I2R resistive coil heating radiates across the air gap into the outer steel casing.

mechanisms.name: Armature & Shaft Continuous Rotation
mechanisms.explanation: Continuous commutation switches coil polarity just before the magnetic neutral plane, sustaining continuous clockwise rotational torque.

assemblySteps.instruction: Press-fit laminated electrical steel armature core onto the center precision shaft using a hydraulic arbor press.
Press copper commutator onto shaft and wind high-temperature copper magnet wire into armature slots; solder coil ends to commutator tangs.
Bond curved permanent ferrite magnets inside the steel housing using structural heat-cured epoxy.
Insert ball bearings into front housing and rear end bell; install spring-loaded carbon brushes in brush holders.
Slide wound rotor assembly into stator housing and crimp rear end bell tabs securely in place.

experiments.title: Reverse DC Voltage Polarity
experiments.consequence: Motor immediately reverses direction of rotation with identical torque curve.
experiments.explanation: In a permanent-magnet brushed DC motor, reversing terminal voltage inverts the direction of current (I) through the armature coils. According to the Lorentz force equation F = I * (L x B), this inverts the torque vector direction.

experiments.title: Brush Wear Disconnection
experiments.consequence: Motor sparks heavily, loses rotational torque, and stalls completely.
experiments.explanation: When carbon brushes lose contact with commutator segments, the electrical circuit opens. The inductive energy in the windings arcs across the air gap, degrading the copper commutator and stopping rotation.

experiments.title: 200% Over-Voltage Runaway
experiments.consequence: Rapid overheating of copper insulation, leading to shorted turns and catastrophic thermal failure.
experiments.explanation: Resistive power loss scales with I²R. Doubling voltage doubles stall current and quadruples thermal power dissipation, vaporizing coil enamel and melting solder joints.
